title: 4.1.7 Q1 Reflection
description: Reflect on your first quarter of programming and connect your experience to the SDLC. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
This one is about your own work, so most of it comes from you rather than from a reading. 4.1.2 (Plan Before You Code) and 4.1.4 (Manual Testing) will help with question 2, and 1.1.6 (The Four Phases) is where the life-cycle phases were introduced. A few sentences per answer is plenty, in your own everyday words.

1. Name one concept from this quarter — variables, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, anything — that you found hardest, and explain how you worked through it.

2. Think about how you would build a small program now. Describe how you would plan it, build it, and test it, and connect that to the software-development life-cycle phases from Week 1. (4.1.2, 4.1.4 and 1.1.6)

3. What is one thing you want to get better at next quarter?

rubric.title: Names a hard concept and describes how they worked through it
rubric.description: Student names a specific Q1 concept they found hard (e.g., 'loops', 'functions', 'arrays') and describes, specifically, how they worked through it — not a generic 'I practiced'. A response like 'I found loops hard so I kept coding until it clicked' does not earn this criterion; a response that names an action ('I wrote the same loop five different ways') does.

rubric.title: Describes a plan → build → test process for a small program
rubric.description: Student describes how they would plan a small program, build it, and test it — in that order or a clearly recognizable sequence. All three stages (planning, building, testing) must be mentioned. A response that only describes coding without planning or testing does not earn this criterion.

rubric.title: Connects reflection to SDLC phases or lived experience this quarter
rubric.description: Student explicitly connects their plan/build/test description (Q2) to the SDLC phases from Week 1, or reflects on a specific moment from this quarter that illustrates one of those phases. A generic 'I know SDLC' mention without any specifics does not earn this criterion.
